answers: Review round 1 at c939145e2b04 (dispatch review in .legion/INFRA-182/review.json): one Important and three Minor findings, all fixed; the four threads replied to and resolved one by one.

proof.criterion: R3 (review finding PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_JF6): the reconnect WARN, and every other line the bus logs naming a NATS URL, never carries the credential, including URL userinfo, which nats.go authenticates with.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary built at this head (cd packages/envoy && go build -o $TMPDIR/listener-new ./cmd/listener) run as a process with PORT=9099 ENVOY_MACHINE_ID=smoke against a real nats-server v2.11.4 on 127.0.0.1:4222 started with --user envoy --pass pw-SECRET-77, then with --auth tok-SECRET-88; the server killed with SIGKILL under the connected listener and started again.
proof.command: NATS_URLS=nats://envoy:pw-SECRET-77@127.0.0.1:4222 listener-new ; kill -9 <nats-server pid> ; sleep 4 ; start nats-server again ; SIGTERM ; count 'pw-SECRET-77' in the log. Same with NATS_URLS=nats://tok-SECRET-88@127.0.0.1:4222. Remote refusal: NATS_URLS=nats://envoy:pw-SECRET-99@nats.example.test:4222 listener-new.
proof.observed: user:password run: 'WARN envoy nats reconnect attempt failed name=envoy servers=nats://127.0.0.1:4222 error="dial tcp 127.0.0.1:4222: connect: connection refused"' then 'INFO envoy nats reconnected name=envoy url=nats://127.0.0.1:4222', 0 occurrences of the password in the whole log. Token run: the same two lines, 0 occurrences. Refusal: 'bus: refusing a NATS server that is not this machine's: nats://nats.example.test:4222 (set ENVOY_ALLOW_REMOTE_NATS=1 to reach it)', exit 1, 0 occurrences.
proof.negativeControl: The binary built the same way from c939145e2b04 (the code round 1 reviewed, exported with git archive) under the same runs: 2 occurrences of the password (servers=nats://envoy:pw-SECRET-77@127.0.0.1:4222 and url=nats://envoy:pw-SECRET-77@127.0.0.1:4222), 2 of the token, and its refusal printed nats://envoy:pw-SECRET-99@nats.example.test:4222.

proof.criterion: R1/R2 after the rebind change (review finding PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_JF8): an unbound durable still answers 503 at once and is rebound, and each rebind and probe read now ends with its context instead of the JetStream handle's 10 s wait.
proof.surface: The same real listener against a JetStream nats-server v2.11.4, the durable recreated with a throwaway nats.go program (ConsumerInfo, DeleteConsumer, AddConsumer with the same config and a fresh nats.NewInbox()); and a throwaway in-package test against a real nats-server without JetStream with $JS.API.> subscribed and never answered, through the real bus.Connect.
proof.command: natsfault recreate ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS listener-smoke ; curl localhost:9099/healthz ; poll until 200 ; natsfault info ; and go test ./cmd/listener/ -run TestZZCtxSmoke (throwaway, deleted)
proof.observed: Baseline 200; recreate new_deliver=_INBOX.En4j4sTswYskIRYg2wQsSS; next request 503 {"error":"durable consumer unavailable: not bound to this listener's subscription","status":"unhealthy"}; one interval later 'self-health probe failed', 'self-health rebuild started', 'self-health recovered'; push_bound=true deliver=_INBOX.En4j4sTswYskIRYg2wQsSS, /healthz 200, 0 ERROR lines. Unanswered JetStream: awaitDurableBound (deadline 1 s) 1.0 s, cancelled at 300 ms 0.30 s with context canceled; durableProbe cancelled at 300 ms 0.30 s, nil.
proof.negativeControl: The same throwaway test before the change: awaitDurableBound 10.0 s against its 1 s deadline, 10.0 s when cancelled at 300 ms, durableProbe 10.0 s when cancelled at 300 ms.

proof.criterion: R4 (review finding PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_JF-): a repair wait reports only the stop that armed it, so a wait a repair cleared never reports the replacement watcher's later stop.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of the new TestAWaitARepairClearedReportsNotTheNextStop and the four existing repair tests, each run against a local nats-server v2.11.4 with JetStream instead of testnats.URL (no container runtime in the pod).
proof.observed: After the fix: TestLocalStaleWait (the reviewer's sequence: stop 1, repair, stop 2, fire wait 1, then wait 2) PASS, wait 1 logs nothing and wait 2 logs the one 'no repair within 1m0s' ERROR; the four existing flows PASS.
proof.negativeControl: Before the fix the same run failed: wait 1 logged 'ERROR test cache watcher was not repaired reason="no repair within 1m0s"' for the second stop moments after it.

proof.criterion: An ordered shutdown writes no ERROR when it cuts a self-health rebuild mid-rebind (found on the real surface this round).
proof.surface: The real listener at 4d392e33/8076e90e against a JetStream nats-server, SIGTERM 0.4 s after the probe found a recreated durable; and the unit test TestRunSelfHealthMonitor_ShutdownCutRebuildLogsNoError.
proof.observed: The real run before the fix logged 'ERROR self-health rebuild failed ... error="rebind durable consumer: context canceled"'. After 91f61c5c the test passes, and the real durable runs at this head log 0 ERROR lines.
proof.negativeControl: The same test before the main.go change failed with that ERROR line.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/internal/bus/reach.go: natsURLWithoutUserinfo; refuseRemoteNATS names the URL without its userinfo
packages/envoy/internal/bus/connect.go: the reconnect WARN's servers and the reconnected line's url have no userinfo; the comment says why

packages/envoy/internal/bus/log_url_test.go (new): the helper table, the reconnect WARN and refusal with user:password, token-only and schemeless URLs, and the reconnected line on a real connection (container)
packages/envoy/cmd/listener/durable.go: durableProbe and awaitDurableBound read under nats.Context; the comments say what bounds each read
packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go: the monitor comment; runSelfHealthMonitor returns without the ERROR when its ctx ended during the rebuild
packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go: the repair wait's callback carries its generation; reportUnrepaired checks it under mu; reportFailedRepair
packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/repair_test.go: the fake keeps every armed callback (fireAt); waitForStopWarns(want); TestAWaitARepairClearedReportsNotTheNextStop; the notice-budget comment
packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md: Fixed entry for the URL userinfo in the bus's log lines
trickyParts: testnats.URL hands out nats://tN:tN@host URLs, so before this fix every container test's reconnected line already wrote a user:password URL; the new container test parses that line's url and requires User == nil.

url.URL.Redacted and nats.Conn.ConnectedUrlRedacted keep a token-only user name, which nats.go sends as the token (connectProto, nats.go:2807-2817), so the helper drops the whole userinfo; an unparseable URL keeps only what follows its last '@'.

nats.go wraps a ctx without a deadline in the JetStream handle's default wait (jsm.go:1791-1796), so durableProbe's reads stay bounded at 10 s while the monitor's cancel cuts them; a cancelled read returns context.Canceled, which durableProbe reads as success, as it always read an unclassified error.
deviations: Beyond the four findings, runSelfHealthMonitor now returns without logging when its ctx ended during a failed rebuild: cutting the rebind on the shutdown's cancel (the point of finding JF8) made an ordered shutdown log 'self-health rebuild failed ... context canceled' at ERROR, observed on the real listener this round.
The unread 'stops' counter of the kvwatch test fake was removed while the fake was rewritten to keep every callback.
discoveredComplexity: go test -race could not run in the pod (no C compiler); envoy-go-race runs it in CI. The container-backed tests (log_url_test.go's reconnected-line test, the new kvwatch test, the repair and listener container tests) run only in CI's envoy-go.
